label: Modal spine A3′: a genuine Grim Reaper patchwork premise and its objection audit
summary: Target: modal spine stage one, premise A3 prime a and horn H2 of the initial-state rival, toward the begun-past premise A3 prime w. Spec: specs/modal-spine-grim-reaper-patchwork.toml. Replaces the near-transcription ReaperAssembly (result c7c9b6d4, kept and marked superseded), whose consequent was a closed Nat claim. ENCODING. TruthCore.Causality.GrimReaperPatchwork adds a world-assembly vocabulary: a ReaperFrame gives, per world and moment, the code on the station's output register and whether it issues. A local piece at station n of a strictly descending sequence of moments c obeys positive trigger, emission, forwarding and admissibility relative to the station at c (n + 1). Two OPEN premises: local pieces (along every descent below a populated moment, adjacent pieces are co-possible from that history) and patchwork (co-possible adjacent pieces glue into one accessible world). The derivation reads a glued world's register codes as station indices (the descent is injective) and composes the verified IndexedSignalReaper.impossible; it does not restate it. Each premise holds without the other in a beginningless integer history (controls 1 and 2: silent registers satisfy patchwork, pivot registers satisfy local pieces), so the conclusion comes only through the derivation. But because no world realizes a whole arrangement (a theorem), the typed patchwork premise for a frame is equivalent to 'adjacent pieces are not all co-possible along any populated descent', founded populated pasts are equivalent to the two premises together, and control 1 holds only because its antecedent fails; the warrant for patchwork must come from the general recombination principle it instantiates. Registers are not tied to ExistsAt or IsAt, so pieces have no existential import (control 2 realizes a pair in an empty world); the bridge from recombining concrete stations to the typed premises is not built. Admissibility constrains only the register at c n but refers to every upstream slot of the descent; it is the clause that excludes a code from a source outside the descent, e.g. at the accumulation point 0 in [0, t]. RESULTS. populatedPastsFoundedOfPatchwork (63217847) gives founded populated pasts (fce4ac74) from the unrestricted premises. Restricted to coinitial descents (running below every earlier moment; e.g. one per past day where the past is metrically infinite, but a coinitial descent may accumulate metrically, as t/2^n in (0, t]), plus countable coinitiality of beginningless populated pasts (checked for ℤ; full ℚ or ℝ line by t - n, open-below half-line by t/2^n), populatedPastsBegunOfPatchwork (61344b75) gives begun populated pasts (0158110b). possiblyBegunOfEarlierGrounds (1e704047) gives A3 prime w from begun populated pasts and A3 prime b (6dd276f0); unlike the founded counterpart this bundle does not carry possible necessary being: BegunComingToBe.Control.zeno satisfies it, the coinitial Reaper premises and countable coinitiality with no necessary individual (control 3). Strength orders: founded populated pasts strengthen begun ones (7ddbe1f8, converse fails in zeno); unrestricted pieces and patchwork strengthen the coinitial ones (90e06025, 8d6b90b9). FAITHFUL TARGET. The Reaper argument is naturally an argument for a begun past: the coinitial premises are silent about pasts with a beginning. The unrestricted premises also exclude contingent presence after the first moment of dense time with a beginning (with ComingToBeHorns control 8; on the WithBot Int analogue zeno no register frame satisfies both, control 3), the setting of Benardete-style paradoxes. OBJECTION AUDIT (Substantive Objection Standard). What would have to differ for the Reaper not to reach a beginningless populated past: (a) no coinitial descent (uncountable coinitiality of time): formal escape, no independent support, not an objection; (b) local pieces fail along it; (c) gluing fails along it. The coinitial premises are purely order-theoretic ((0, t] and (-infinity, t] are order-isomorphic), so objections for metrically finite open-below pasts are objections to the typed premises. KEPT (1), FLRW: standard FLRW Big Bang cosmology has time open below (the singularity is not a moment); a populated FLRW history has no begun moment and countable coinitiality holds there, so by the theorem the coinitial local-pieces or patchwork premise fails if such a history is accessible; accepted physical theory treats such models as possible. It is a cost of the necessity premises and of begun populated pasts (0158110b), not of the possibility premise A3 prime w. Begun populated pasts also exclude empty beginningless time before a first event (BegunAt concerns the shared time order). KEPT (2), conditional on a separate commitment C (populated continuous time with a first moment is possible; A3 prime w permits but does not assert it): Benardete parity. Anyone admitting C must reject local pieces or gluing for t, t/2, ... in [0, t]; in (0, t] the same descent is coinitial with pieces in the same slots, differing only at an instant hosting no piece, where admissibility bites. So, given C, the typed coinitial premises are doubtful for open-below finite pasts. The parity step is an analyst argument, not machine-checked. Not substantiated, for a philosophical, metrically restricted reading (slots of bounded-below length) that has no Lean counterpart until the metric version exists: transfer to metrically infinite pasts (needs the diagnosis that gluing fails for every infinite descending arrangement; no independent reason recorded); the global-compatibility reply of the 367 audit, located as a fork: adjacent-pair witnesses cannot agree on their shared registers (overlapAgreeingWitnessesImpossible, checked lemma), so (i) if gluing requires value agreement on overlaps the local premise fails along every descent and the argument does not start, and (ii) if gluing duplicates stations with their rules, cyclic failures do not apply to a descent, and the one acyclic candidate is the accumulating Benardete chain (given C, and a gluing failure only if those pieces are possible); for non-accumulating descents no case is recorded, so under (ii) and the metric reading it is unsupported; the unsatisfiable-pair diagnosis (reading lead, no recorded mechanism; joint unsatisfiability is common ground and does not locate the failure); the old 'dropping assumptions may dissolve the contradiction' (removed: the needed rules are exact, each shown necessary by IndexedSignalReaper.Controls); the earlier agent description of the Reaper as 'one special case' that might not generalize (withdrawn: no difference named). Plain verdict: two objections to the typed premises are kept (FLRW; Benardete parity given C). For the philosophical reading (concrete stations duplicated with their rules, slots of bounded-below length, a metrically infinite past only), which has no Lean counterpart yet, no substantive objection is identified. All premises remain OPEN; their support is the defeasible recombination case in docs/notes/causal-finitism-367.md. The theorems show only what accepting the premises costs. Nothing is attributed to Koons or Pruss. No premise is established.
blocker: All Reaper premises are OPEN. Next tests: (1) a metric version (stations in slots of at least a fixed length) concluding that no populated past is metrically infinite, to separate metrically infinite pasts from open-below finite ones, and its connection to the spine (it does not by itself give begun pasts); (2) read and record the unsatisfiable-pair diagnosis and the global-compatibility reply with their mechanisms, if either is selected as a warrant question; (3) a begun-past counterpart of state-causal finitism.
